'''Patricia S. Hu''' is a [[Taiwanese-American]] public servant who was the fourth director of the [[Bureau of Transportation Statistics]] at the [[United States Department of Transportation]] from 2011 to 2025, the first woman to hold that position.<ref>{{cite web |title=Staff Directory |url=https://www.bts.gov/learn-about-bts-and-our-work/about-bts/staff-directory |website=bts.gov |publisher=Bureau of Transportation Statistics |access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref> She was previously the director of the Center for Transportation Analysis at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]].

== Career ==
Hu received statistics degrees from the [[National Chengchi University]] and the [[University of Guelph]].<ref>[https://www.transportation.gov/government/traffic-records/patricia-s-hu Patricia S. Hu] at U.S. Department of Transportation web site</ref>  She was chairman of the [[Transportation Research Board]].<ref name="Bloomberg">{{cite web |title=Patricia S Hu Director/Assoc Administrator, (US) Bureau of Transportation Stats |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/person/17453850 |website=Bloomberg |access-date=13 March 2021}}</ref>

She worked as a biostatistician for [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], and then joined Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) in 1982.<ref name="ornl">{{cite web |title=ORNL's Energy Division's Hu receives three committee appointments |date=May 3, 1996 |url=https://www.ornl.gov/news/ornls-energy-divisions-hu-receives-three-committee-appointments |website=Oak Ridge National Laboratory |access-date=13 March 2021}}</ref>
She was director of ORNL's Center for Transportation Analysis for nine years, and co-authored many of its annual ''Summary of Travel Trends: Nationwide Personal Travel Survey'' bulletins, detailing household vehicle travel patterns and usage.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hu|first1=Patricia S.|last2=Young|first2=Jennifer R.|date=December 1999|title=Summary of Travel Trends: 1999 Nationwide Personal Transportation Survey|url=https://permanent.fdlp.gov/gpo68796/trends_report.pdf|journal=Nationwide Personal Transportation Survey|publisher=U.S. Department of Transportation|pages=142|via=FDLP}}</ref> In addition, she co-authored various journal articles investigating the relationship between aging and car crashes, and the different risk factors found among older male and female drivers.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hu|first1=P. S.|last2=Young|first2=J. R.|last3=Lu|first3=An|date=1993-08-01|title=Highway crash rates and age-related driver limitations: Literature review and evaluation of data bases|url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/10149328/|language=English|doi=10.2172/10149328|osti=10149328|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hu|first1=Patricia S|last2=Trumble|first2=David A|last3=Foley|first3=Daniel J|last4=Eberhard|first4=John W|last5=Wallace|first5=Robert B|date=1998-09-01|title=Crash risks of older drivers: a panel data analysis|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001457598000190|journal=Accident Analysis & Prevention|language=en|volume=30|issue=5|pages=569–581|doi=10.1016/S0001-4575(98)00019-0|pmid=9678211|issn=0001-4575|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hu|first1=Patricia S.|url=https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/13458|title=Driving Decisions and Vehicle Crashes Among Older Drivers|last2=Lu|first2=An|last3=Trumble|first3=David|publisher=Oak Ridge National Laboratory|year=1995}}</ref>

Hu started at the Bureau of Transportation Statistics as Director in 2011. It is a civil service position. "Hu has led many applied research projects, published extensively, and received the TRB Pyke Johnson Award in 1984."<ref name="TRNews">{{cite journal |title=Profile: Patricia S. Hu, Bureau of Transportation Statistics |journal=TR News: Women and Gender in Transportation |date=2019 |issue=May/June |page=48 |url=http://onlinepubs.trb.org/onlinepubs/trnews/trnews321.pdf |access-date=13 March 2021}}</ref><ref>[http://www.trb.org/AboutTRB/JohnsonAward.aspx Pyke Johnson Award] at NASEM web site</ref> She has also received the [[YMCA]]'s Tribute to Women Award, and the [[Association for Women in Science]] Award.<ref name="AMSTATNEWS">{{cite journal |title=Meet Bureau of Transportation Statistics Director Patricia Hu |journal=Amstatnews |date=1 July 2011 |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2011/07/01/hu-july11/ |access-date=13 March 2021}}</ref>

As the Director of the BTS, Hu worked to increase the efficiency of the agency by better leveraging the sharing of [[big data]], such as data from the [[Waze]] app to mine highway safety information in order to best position emergency vehicles to respond to accidents quickly and efficiently.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-10-03|title='How do we do better?' Chief data officers see hiring challenges persist|url=https://federalnewsnetwork.com/big-data/2019/10/how-do-we-do-better-chief-data-officers-see-hiring-challenges-persist/|access-date=2021-03-14|website=Federal News Network|language=en-US}}</ref>
